parsed.explanation: The finiteness in this write-up rests entirely on the "finite blocker" fact. The objection correctly identifies the fatal gap: after inserting c into the branch, every later selected set F_D must be disjoint from the current label, hence cannot contain c, so the claimed "next occurrence" of c along the modified branch is unjustified; the contraction argument collapses. Worse, the fact is outright false: F_k = {x_1,...,x_k, y_k} is pairwise intersecting yet {y_1,...,y_k, x_{k+1}} is a minimal transversal for every k, giving infinitely many. So no local edit repairs it; genuine large-prime erasure (using a_n's size and minimality, not mere pairwise intersection) is nowhere in the text.
